title: [BUG] Bedrock Mantle base-path table only handles openai.gpt-5.*, mis-routing xai.grok-4.3 (and every third-party model) to /v1
body:
### Checks

- [x] I have updated to the lastest minor and patch version of Strands
- [x] I have checked the documentation and this is not expected behavior
- [x] I have searched ./issues and there are no duplicates of my issue

### SDK Language

TypeScript

### Strands Version

Reported against current `main` / latest published `@strands-agents/sdk`. Exact version not captured from the reporter — the routing defect below is present on `main` as of this filing.

### Language Runtime Version

Not captured from the reporter (Node.js).

### Operating System

Not captured from the reporter.

### Installation Method

npm

### Steps to Reproduce

Reported by a user attempting to reach `xai.grok-4.3` through the Bedrock Mantle endpoint in `us-east-1` (`https://bedrock-mantle.us-east-1.api.aws`).

```ts
import { OpenAIModel } from '@strands-agents/sdk/models/openai'

const model = new OpenAIModel({
  modelId: 'xai.grok-4.3',
  bedrockMantleConfig: { region: 'us-east-1' },
})

await model.stream([{ role: 'user', content: [{ text: 'hello' }] }])
```

The model id is valid and servable-by-catalog: `GET /v1/models` on the same endpoint returns `xai.grok-4.3` with `"status":"available"`, so this is not a typo'd or unavailable model id.

The reporter also exercised the three routes directly with `curl` to isolate the SDK from the service:

| Route | Payload shape | HTTP | Response |
|---|---|---|---|
| `/v1/chat/completions` | Chat Completions | 400 | `{"error":{"code":"validation_error","message":"model 'xai.grok-4.3' isn't supported on this route","type":"invalid_request_error"}}` |
| `/openai/v1/chat/completions` | Chat Completions | 500 | `{"error":{"code":"internal_server_error","message":"The server had an error while processing your request. Sorry about that!","type":"server_error"}}` |
| `/openai/v1/responses` | Responses API | 500 | same `internal_server_error` body |

Control case, same account, same credentials, same session: `google.gemma-4-31b` returns valid completions on **`/openai/v1/chat/completions`** and **`/openai/v1/responses`**. That rules out credentials, account permissions, and client code.

### Expected Behavior

Two separate expectations, because there are two separate defects here — one ours, one not.

1. `OpenAIModel` + `bedrockMantleConfig` should route a non-OpenAI-family Mantle model id (`xai.*`, `google.*`, `anthropic.*`) to the base path Mantle actually serves it from. It should not construct a request against a route the service will reject with `validation_error`.
2. A model advertised as `"status":"available"` by `GET /v1/models` should be invocable on at least one route.

### Actual Behavior

**Defect 1 (SDK, actionable here): the Mantle base-path table only special-cases `openai.gpt-5.*`, so every third-party model id falls through to `/v1` — the route that 400s.**

`strands-ts/src/models/openai/mantle.ts`:

```ts
const OPENAI_PATH_MODEL_PREFIXES = ['openai.gpt-5.'] as const

export function bedrockMantleBaseUrl(region: string, modelId: string): string {
  const suffix = OPENAI_PATH_MODEL_PREFIXES.some((prefix) => modelId.startsWith(prefix)) ? '/openai/v1' : '/v1'
  return `https://bedrock-mantle.${region}.api.aws${suffix}`
}
```

`xai.grok-4.3` does not start with `openai.gpt-5.`, so it resolves to `/v1` — and `/v1/chat/completions` is precisely the route that returns `model 'xai.grok-4.3' isn't supported on this route`. The SDK cannot currently be pointed at `/openai/v1` for this model either, since `bedrockMantleConfig` rejects a caller-supplied `clientConfig.baseURL` (validated in `mantle.test.ts`, "throws when `clientConfig.baseURL` is set alongside `bedrockMantleConfig`"). There is no supported escape hatch.

The reporter's own control case is the proof that the table is wrong, not just incomplete: `google.gemma-4-31b` **works** on `/openai/v1`, but the SDK would route it to `/v1` for the same reason. So the mis-routing is not specific to Grok — it applies to every non-`openai.gpt-5.*` id, and it is currently masked only because those models aren't documented as supported yet (#3563).

The comment in `mantle.ts` states the operative rule correctly ("the base path is keyed by model family, not API surface") but the prefix list encodes only the OpenAI families that existed when it was written.

**Defect 2 (Mantle service-side, not fixable in this repo): `/openai/v1/*` 500s for `xai.grok-4.3`.**

Once routed to `/openai/v1`, Grok returns `internal_server_error` on both Chat Completions and Responses, while Gemma succeeds on the same routes with the same credentials. That is a serving-side problem with this specific model, either a catalog mis-registration (advertised `available`, not actually servable) or a backend fault. Fixing Defect 1 will **not** make `xai.grok-4.3` work; it will change a 400 into a 500 until the service side is resolved. Worth cutting a separate ticket to the Bedrock Mantle service team, and worth confirming Grok is servable before wiring it up here — otherwise SDK-side support cannot be integ-tested.

### Additional Context

Parity: the Python SDK has the identical defect at `strands-py/src/strands/models/_openai_bedrock.py`:

```python
_OPENAI_PATH_MODEL_PREFIXES: tuple[str, ...] = ("openai.gpt-5.",)

def _resolve_mantle_base_path(model_id: str) -> str:
    if model_id.startswith(_OPENAI_PATH_MODEL_PREFIXES):
        return "/openai/v1"
    return "/v1"
```

Any fix should land in both SDKs to preserve parity.

Related history on this same base-path logic, all of which suggests the prefix-matching approach is fragile enough to be worth replacing rather than extending:

- #3279 — `[BUG] OpenAIModel Bedrock Mantle base URL is wrong for the Responses API (hits /v1/responses)` (closed)
- #2629 — `bedrock_mantle_config builds wrong base_url for OpenAI Responses models (missing /openai path segment)` (closed)
- #3388 — `OpenAIModel (Responses, TypeScript) sends invalid assistant history shape, rejected by Bedrock Mantle` (closed)

This is the fourth bug filed against Mantle base-URL/route derivation.

### Possible Solution

Scoped to Defect 1 only.

The narrow fix is to add the third-party families to the prefix list so they resolve to `/openai/v1`:

```ts
const OPENAI_PATH_MODEL_PREFIXES = ['openai.gpt-5.', 'xai.', 'google.', 'anthropic.'] as const
```

That is a one-line change, mirrored in Python, and it makes the confirmed-working case (`google.gemma-4-31b` on `/openai/v1`) actually reachable through the SDK. But it keeps the design that has now produced four bugs: a hardcoded allowlist of prefixes that must be updated every time Mantle onboards a family, where the failure mode is a confusing service-side 400 rather than a clear client-side error.

Two alternatives worth weighing during triage:

1. **Invert the default.** `/openai/v1` appears to be the general case and `/v1` the exception (`openai.gpt-oss-*`). Encoding the exceptions instead of the rule shrinks the list that needs maintenance and makes new families work by default.
2. **Fail loudly on unrecognized families.** If the model id matches no known Mantle family, throw a client-side error naming the id and the supported prefixes rather than silently building a URL that the service will reject. That converts an opaque `validation_error` from Mantle into an actionable message, which is what the reporter needed here.

Either way, extending the allowlist without also deciding on the default is likely to produce bug number five.

Also worth considering: whether `bedrockMantleConfig`'s hard rejection of `clientConfig.baseURL` should relax to a documented override. The validation is sound as a default (it prevents accidentally unsigned or mis-pointed requests), but with no escape hatch, a routing-table gap is a hard block rather than a workaround-able annoyance.

### Related Issues

#3563 (feature request: Mantle-API support for Anthropic, Google and Grok models). This issue is the bug half of that request: the routing table silently mis-routes those families today rather than rejecting them, so the failure surfaces as an opaque service 400.
